page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with 12 shared vCPUs on an Intel x86_64 architecture, featuring 6 physical cores and 2 threads per core running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. Graphics processing is handled by two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 700 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier for LLM inference prompt processing, achieving 8665.1 tokens per second with a small 135M model and 613.27 tokens per second with a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds are strong, reaching 260.3 tokens per second for the 135M model and 32.35 tokens per second for the 7B model. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores, fall within the average range. The shared CPU allocation and 2.0 GHz clock speed represent a tradeoff, resulting in average single-core performance compared to dedicated compute instances.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high density of GPU resources and system memory relative to its shared CPU allocation, making it a viable option for workloads that require parallel GPU acceleration without needing dedicated high-frequency CPU cores. Appropriate workloads include small to medium LLM inference, parallel data processing, GPU-accelerated rendering, and memory-intensive database operations.
